transcript: This week, I saw Magnificent Bird and Book of Travelers at Playwrights Horizons. Currently being performed in rep, they're a pair of complimentary pieces by Gabriel Kahane, both of which are collection of songs and autobiographical anecdotes which take the form of something between a monologue, a conversation, and stand-up. In Book of Travelers, Gabriel describes experiences he had while traveling across the United States via Amtrak for 13 days. Magnificent Bird is about a year that he spent completely unplugged from technology. Both very interesting pieces — Gabriel is a great pianist with a knack for interesting chord progressions, and his songs range from melodic and familiar to more poetic and understated. The non-musical material is similarly precise but the whole vibe of the show is very casual, very cozy and intimate which feels apt for the themes is raised in the show such as community vs isolation, grief, and connection. If this seems up your alley, you can catch these shows at Playwrights Horizons through October 13th. With that, another program for my collection.
